title: Chapter 8: Identification of Common Trade Tools

blocks.content: 1. Introduction

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Trade tools are classified based on their functional usage into hand, striking, cutting, holding, measuring, and power tools.
Striking tools like hammers and mallets apply force, while cutting tools like chisels and hacksaws remove material.
Holding and clamping tools secure workpieces firmly to ensure safe and precise operations.
Accurate measuring tools are vital for maintaining required dimensions and tolerances in trade jobs.
Routine care, maintenance, and strict adherence to safety rules prevent tool damage and workplace injuries.

blocks.content: Tools are instruments used to perform specific mechanical tasks such as cutting, shaping, measuring, holding, or assembling materials.
In technical trades like fitter, electrician, welder, mechanic, and carpenter, tools are essential for efficient and accurate work.
Correct identification of tools helps workers choose the right tool for the job, improves efficiency, prevents accidents,
and protects materials and machines from damage.
2. Classification of Trade Tools
Workshop tools are classified according to their function.
Hand Tools – Operated manually without power (hammer, screwdriver)
Cutting Tools – Used to remove material (hacksaw, chisel)
Measuring Tools – Used for accurate measurement (vernier caliper, steel rule)
Holding Tools – Used to grip workpieces (bench vice, clamp)
Striking Tools – Used to apply force (ball peen hammer)
Power Tools – Operated by electricity or motors (electric drill)
3. Hand Tools
Hand tools are the most commonly used tools in workshops and require manual effort.
Hammer – Used for striking and driving nails
Screwdriver – Used for tightening or loosening screws
Spanner/Wrench – Used for tightening or loosening nuts and bolts
Pliers – Used for gripping and bending wires
File – Used for smoothing rough metal surfaces
4. Striking Tools
Striking tools apply impact force.
Ball Peen Hammer – Used in metalworking
Sledgehammer – Used for heavy striking work
Mallet – Used for striking without damaging surfaces

5. Cutting Tools
Cutting tools remove material from a workpiece.
Hacksaw – Used for cutting metal rods and pipes
Chisel – Used for cutting or shaping metal or wood
Drill Bit – Used for making holes
Snips/Shears – Used for cutting thin sheet metal
6. Holding and Clamping Tools
These tools hold workpieces firmly during operations.
Bench Vice – Holds work securely on a workbench
C‑Clamp – Temporarily clamps objects together
Pipe Wrench – Grips and turns pipes
Locking Pliers – Provides strong gripping force
7. Measuring Tools
Measuring tools ensure accuracy.

rows: Deliver impact force for driving or shaping

blocks.content: Steel Rule – Measures length
Measuring Tape – Measures long distances
Vernier Caliper – Measures internal and external dimensions precisely
Micrometer – Measures very small thickness or diameter
8. Power Tools
Power tools are operated using electrical or mechanical power.
Electric Drill – Used for drilling holes
Angle Grinder – Used for cutting and grinding metal
Power Saw – Used for cutting wood or metal
Impact Wrench – Used for tightening bolts
9. Care and Maintenance of Tools
Clean tools after use.
Store tools properly in toolboxes.
Keep cutting tools sharp.
Inspect tools regularly for damage.
Protect tools from rust.
10. Safety Rules While Using Tools

items: Identification of specific striking and cutting tools based on their features is frequently tested.
Distinguishing between holding tools (e.g., bench vice) and clamping tools (e.g., C-clamp) is a recurring exam objective.
Safety rules and proper maintenance practices for power and hand tools carry significant weight in trade competitive exams.

blocks.content: Always use the correct tool for the job.
Inspect tools before use.
Wear Personal Protective Equipment (PPE).
Never use damaged tools.
Store tools safely after use.
Exam-Oriented Key Points
Hand tools operate without electricity.
Hacksaw is used for cutting metal.
Bench vice holds workpieces securely.
Vernier caliper is used for precise measurement.
Proper tool maintenance improves safety and efficiency.
